plain.text: Two days before the Passover, the chief priests and elders plotted to arrest Jesus secretly and kill him. In Bethany, a woman poured very expensive perfume on Jesus' head. The disciples complained about the waste; it could have been sold for the poor. Jesus said she had done a beautiful thing, preparing his body for burial, and she would be remembered wherever the gospel is preached. Then Judas Iscariot went to the chief priests and agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.

The disciples prepared the Passover meal. As they ate, Jesus said one of them would betray him. They were deeply saddened. Judas asked, Surely not I, Rabbi? and Jesus said, You have said so. Then Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it and said, Take and eat; this is my body. He took the cup and said, Drink from it, all of you. This is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. After singing a hymn they went out to the Mount of Olives.

Jesus said they would all fall away that night. Peter insisted he never would, but Jesus said that before the rooster crowed Peter would deny him three times. At Gethsemane Jesus took Peter, James and John and said his soul was overwhelmed with sorrow to the point of death. He fell on his face and prayed: My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me. Yet not as I will, but as you will. Three times he prayed, and three times he found the disciples asleep.

Judas arrived with a crowd armed with swords and clubs, and greeted Jesus with a kiss as the signal. They seized Jesus. One of his followers cut off a servant's ear, but Jesus said, Put your sword back; all who draw the sword will die by the sword. He could call on more than twelve legions of angels, but the Scriptures must be fulfilled. Then all the disciples deserted him and fled.

They took Jesus to Caiaphas the high priest, where the council looked for false evidence against him. Jesus stayed silent. The high priest demanded under oath: tell us if you are the Christ, the Son of God. Jesus said, You have said so, and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven. The high priest tore his clothes and cried blasphemy. They said he deserved death, spat on him and struck him.

Peter was sitting in the courtyard. A servant girl said he had been with Jesus, but he denied it. Another said the same, and he denied it with an oath. Later others said his accent gave him away, and he swore, I do not know the man! Immediately a rooster crowed. Peter remembered Jesus' words, went outside and wept bitterly.

summary.bigIdea: On the night he is betrayed, Jesus gives his disciples the bread and cup of the new covenant and chooses his Father's will, even as his friends fail him.
points: A woman anoints Jesus, and Judas agrees to betray him.
At the Last Supper Jesus speaks of his body and his blood poured out for many.
In Gethsemane he prays, not as I will, but as you will.
summary.reflection: Jesus prayed, not as I will, but as you will. Is there an area of your life where that prayer is hard to pray?
